sentences.text: The capacity picture is built from demand forecasts, observed traffic, airport resource status, airspace constraints, and weather products that are updated throughout the tactical planning horizon.
The Demand Prediction Service, also known as Marlinstone, generates the demand forecast used by the Regional Flow Platform.
The Weather Ingest Gateway, also known as Orchard, normalizes external and local meteorological feeds before they are used in operational capacity calculations.
The Demand Prediction Service receives filed flight information through the Flight Data Exchange and compares it with the current operating schedule held by the Airline Interface Adapter.
Flight Intent Message updates are treated as the primary indicator of operator intent when the system detects a material difference from the published schedule.
The Demand Prediction Service uses recent conformance history, aircraft rotation timing, and known bank structures to estimate arrival and departure loads by planning interval.
The Sector Load Monitor contributes airspace demand indicators so that airport capacity is not assessed independently of nearby sector saturation.
The Capacity Assessment Module combines demand projections with the Airport Capacity Plan to determine whether a published Airport Acceptance Rate remains feasible.

The Weather Ingest Gateway accepts aviation forecasts, radar-derived precipitation fields, lightning alerts, wind forecasts, ceiling and visibility forecasts, and runway condition weather inputs from approved sources.
Each weather feed is checked for source identity, issue time, valid time, spatial reference, and unit consistency before it is made available to the Regional Flow Platform.
The Time Synchronization Service provides the reference clock used to compare forecast issue times with operational decision times.
When a forecast product arrives late or fails validation, the Weather Ingest Gateway marks the feed as degraded rather than silently excluding it from the operational picture.
The Meteorology Briefing Officer reviews degraded weather inputs when they affect capacity assumptions for the next planning period.
Weather impacts are translated into capacity modifiers for runway configuration, arrival spacing, departure spacing, surface movement constraints, and approach sector availability.
The North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter receive runway-specific capacity values after the Capacity Assessment Module applies the current wind, visibility, and precipitation assumptions.
Surface constraints from the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor are correlated with weather-driven taxi speed assumptions before the Ramp Movement Board is updated.
The Airport Duty Manager may request a manual capacity review when local observations differ materially from the automated weather interpretation.
The Regional Flow Manager uses the Common Situation Display to compare forecast demand, assessed capacity, and any active Ground Delay Program effects in one operational view.
Forecast confidence is recorded as a confidence class, a probability value where provided by the source, a valid time range, and the forecast horizon used for the calculation.
The confidence record also stores the originating feed, the processing time, the transformation version, and any manual override applied by the Meteorology Briefing Officer.
Low-confidence weather forecasts remain visible to users, but the Capacity Assessment Module flags the associated capacity values as provisional.

When confidence decreases below the configured threshold, the Alert Distribution Hub notifies the Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, and Airline Operations Coordinator that the capacity picture may change.
All forecast confidence changes, feed quality changes, and capacity recalculations are written to the Collaborative Decision Log with synchronized timestamps.
The Audit Event Ledger retains the trace from incoming forecast product to capacity value so that the Performance Analytics Warehouse can reconstruct the decision basis after operations.
